description: Diurnal inputs of AT-041h (src/atlas/ml/diurnal_features.py). Same format and checks as madrid_partitions.json; added to the AT-041d terms. Every term is an ICA band; only the inputs are new. Fitted quantities (climatology, rho) come from training rows only.

variables.rationale: Training-period (2019-2023) median NO2 of the station at the local hour and day type (Laborable Mon-Fri / Sabado / Domingo; holidays not encoded) of the target hour: what this station usually reads at that hour on that kind of day. A table of 24 stations x 24 hours x 3 day types computed from training rows only. Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.

no2_clim_valid + (no2_last - usual value of the station at the hour and day type of no2_last), floored at 0 ug/m3: today's departure from the station's usual value, carried forward unchanged to the target hour (persistence of the anomaly projected on the diurnal cycle). The floor only says a concentration cannot be negative. Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.

no2_clim_valid x (no2_last + 6) / (usual value at the hour of no2_last + 6): the same projection with the departure as a ratio (the diurnal cycle scales the level). The 6 ug/m3 offset keeps a near-zero usual value from blowing the ratio up; it is the measurement-uncertainty scale of the NO2 terms (15 % of 40), a scale and not a fitted constant. Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.

no2_clim_valid + rho x (no2_last - usual value at the hour of no2_last), floored at 0, rho = least-squares slope (no intercept) of the target's departure on no2_last's departure over the complete training rows: a linear persistence-plus-diurnal expectation in which only the share rho of today's departure survives to the target hour. One number fitted on training rows only. Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.

NO2 of the same station 24 h before the target hour (key t+h-24h; for h = 6 that is the finished hour [t-18h, t-17h)): what happened yesterday at the hour being forecast. It carries the diurnal cycle and the multi-day persistence of episodes at once, without any fitted quantity. Missing if that hour has no valid value. Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.

NO2 of the same station 168 h before the target hour (same local hour and weekday last week, key t+h-168h): the weekly pattern of traffic emissions. Missing if that hour has no valid value. Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.

Mean NO2 of the station over the 24 finished hours [t-24h, t), with at least 18 valid hours (75 % data capture, Directive 2008/50/EC Annex VII for daily aggregation): the level of the last day, a marker of multi-day accumulation episodes. Bands of the hourly ICA scale used as a reading of the level, not as a daily limit value. Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.

Maximum hourly NO2 of the station over the 24 finished hours [t-24h, t), with at least 18 valid hours: the worst hour of the last day (whether yesterday's rush-hour peak reached Regular or worse). Terms = the ICA bands of the target with the shoulders of no2_last (15 % of each breakpoint: 6, 13.5, 18 ug/m3; see madrid_partitions.json for the source and its caveats), so a rule reads in the target's own language, e.g. 'no2_expected_valid IS Regular'.
